In recent years, digitalization has shifted from being an optional add-on to a cornerstone of the energy sector, driving transformative changes; and 2025 will be no different.

But the rapid digitalization of energy systems also brings complex risks like cybersecurity threats, data bias and ethical concerns that must be proactively managed. The European Union's experience, which saw over 200 cyberattacks on energy infrastructure in 2023 alone, highlights the urgent need for resilient energy systems. 

Protecting critical energy services from these vulnerabilities requires robust governance and security measures. Global collaborative initiatives like the G20's Data20 are steps toward promoting better data governance to support AI-driven innovation and the SDGs.

Moving forward, the challenge will be balancing digital innovation with safeguards to protect infrastructure and ensure equitable access.  

Learn how robust governance can ensure AI and digitalization strengthen—not compromise—the energy transition in 2025, safeguarding infrastructure, data integrity, and equitable access. 👉 bit.ly/seh-bulletin-2025
